steps.title: PINGPONG: A BENCHMARK FOR ROLE-PLAYING LAN-GUAGE MODELS WITH USER EMULATION AND MULTI-MODEL EVALUATION

core_judgments: The novelty of the proposed 'LLM-as-a-judge' approach is not clearly established.

The paper does not sufficiently articulate how its evaluation methodology differs from existing role-playing benchmarks, particularly those that also assess conversational abilities, albeit in single-turn settings.

Overall, while the benchmark may offer incremental improvements in realism and evaluation setup, the paper would benefit from more clearly delineating its novel contributions and providing stronger evidence that its approach yields new insights beyond those available in prior literature.

conclusion: The central contribution of this paper is a benchmark/framework for evaluating the role-playing abilities of language models using a three-agent, LM-driven setup (player, interrogator, and multiple judges) with dynamically generated queries and multi-model evaluation. Closest prior work is MORTISE in “Enhancing Role-playing Systems through Aggressive Queries: Evaluation and Improvement,” which already introduces a designed system to benchmark and stress-test role-playing LLMs via adversarial, role-relevant queries and an adversarial dataset for evaluation and improvement, directly overlapping with the submission’s goal of benchmarking role adherence. Other benchmarks such as SocialBench, RoleLLM/RoleBench, CharacterEval, and ECHO likewise already provide role-playing evaluation datasets and protocols, including multi-turn dialogues and automatic or GPT-based evaluators. Relative to these, the submission’s main deltas are operational design choices: making the benchmark fully dynamic (LM-generated interrogator prompts each run), structuring evaluation as a three-agent interaction, averaging multiple judge models to reduce bias, and using per-turn scalar scores with criteria like character consistency and entertainment. These are useful refinements but remain largely at the level of protocol engineering around an already-established task and setup. Overall, the central contribution is not novel enough to constitute a genuine advance.
